question: Why should the devotee’s requests not be considered destined to fail?
premises: The devotee has not gone to excess until now.
Requests and similar appeals have been made.
Such appeals do not deserve fruitlessness.
inference: Because the devotee has not been excessive, requests should not be deemed fruitless.
uncertainties: The phrase adhikām itaṃ mayā is syntactically compressed.
plain_english: Until today I have not gone to excess, so my requests and the like do not deserve to be fruitless.
